title: Etale local rings on charts and flat morphisms of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X,Y$ algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ (where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed), write $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ for the stalk of the structure sheaf of the small etale site. If $e:T\to X$ is an etale map from a scheme and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ lifts $\bar x$, with image $t\in T$, there are canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}\cong\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}\cong\mathcal O_{T,t}^{\mathrm{sh}}$. The last ring is the strict henselization of the local ring at $t$, for the residue-field embedding furnished by $\bar t$ [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]. For a morphism $g:X\to Y$, put $\bar y=g\bar x$. The induced map $\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}\to\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ is a local ring homomorphism, and it is flat if and only if $g$ is flat at the image $x\in|X|$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Here $g$ is flat at $x$ when there are etale maps $U\to X$, $V\to Y$ from schemes, a morphism $h:U\to V$ compatible with $g$, and a point $u\in U$ over $x$ at which $h$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]; this does not depend on the choices. Etaleness means [def-weil-etale-morphism] on scheme charts; a local homomorphism maps the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal.

source.place: Tags 04KG (definition-etale-local-rings), 04KF (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), and 04NG (lemma-flat-at-point-etale-local-rings). proof.text: For strictLocalChartComparison apply lem-sfb-space-chart-germ-cocone to the existing ring cocone of stalkModel s x. It supplies a natural transformation γ on the actual affine pointed scheme-neighbourhood diagram, its germ formula, and a compatible small refinement for every neighbourhood. By lem-sfb-space-chart-germ-cocone-is-colimit this cocone is colimiting. IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso compares it with the existing scheme colimit; precompose with smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso to get the ring equivalence from strictHenselizationRing. Its coprojection identity is exactly the requested germ formula after the inverse comparison in strictLocalSchemeGerm cancels. For uniqueness, for each affine N choose the supplied compatible M,a. The two candidate equivalences have equal composites with the N-germ by their stipulated formulas. Cancel the small comparison isomorphism and apply colimit hom-ext to deduce equality of the ring homomorphisms and hence of the ring equivalences. This proves both existence and uniqueness without using either strict-henselization presentations or flatness.

source.place: Tag 04KF, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring, first equality; Tag 04K2, lemma-stalk-pullback (4), direct proof on pointed neighbourhoods.

proof.text: For any scheme $T$ and geometric point $\bar t$ centered at $t$, restrict the stalk colimit to affine pointed neighbourhoods by [lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal]. Choose an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}D\subset T$ containing $t$, with prime $\mathfrak p$ and separable residue closure $K\subset\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] the resulting ring colimit is canonically the colimit of etale residue triples over $(D,\mathfrak p,K)$, preserving its section maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] this colimit $C$ is local and evaluation $\psi:C\to K$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak m_C$. Clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $D_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ through the germ map. Applying [lem-sbc-etale-triples-localized-strict-henselization] to the cocone of triples over $(D,\mathfrak p,K)$ with $b:D\to C$ the leg of $\operatorname{Spec}D$, the ring $C$ is a strict henselization of $D_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{T,t}$ in the sense of [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], with $D\to D_{\mathfrak p}\to C$ equal to $b$; since $D\to D_{\mathfrak p}$ is a localization, the map $\mathcal O_{T,t}\to C$ is the germ map. By [lem-sc-etale-triples-colimit-is-strict-henselization] for the local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ at its maximal ideal, the triples colimit over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is also such a strict henselization; two vertices of universal colimit cocones of the same diagram are isomorphic as $\mathcal O_{T,t}$-algebras, so $C\cong\mathcal O_{T,t}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ as in the statement. This proves the second claimed isomorphism with the prescribed residue embedding. In particular the evaluation $\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}\to\Omega$ has kernel its unique maximal ideal. Together with step 1 this gives the same assertion for $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$.

source.place: Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), via Tags 03PQ and 04GW; the residue evaluation is Tag 04GP, as stated in the triples node.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $b:V\to Y$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and then $a:U\to X$, $h:U\to V$ with $bh=ga$, $a$ surjective etale, by the unconditional presentation-existence clause of [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts]. Since $a$ is surjective, the scheme $U\times_{X,\bar x}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is nonempty; the image in $U$ of one of its points is a point $u$ over $x$. The lemma [lem-sfb-etale-geometric-point-specified-lift] lifts the fixed $\bar x$ to $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ centered at this $u$; put $\bar v=h\bar u$ and $v=h(u)$. More generally the same lifting applies to any compatible chart and any of its points over $x$. Write $A=\mathcal O_{V,v}$, $B=\mathcal O_{U,u}$, $A^{\mathrm{sh}}=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$ and $B^{\mathrm{sh}}=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ by steps 1 and 2. The induced square $A\to A^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $B\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$, with vertical arrows induced by $h$ and $g$, commutes: the map $A^{\mathrm{sh}}\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ sends the germ of a regular function $s$ on a pointed etale $V$-neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar v$ to the germ of $\mathrm{pr}_1^*s$ on the pointed etale $U$-neighbourhood $(W\times_VU,(\bar w,\bar u))$, which is pointed because $\bar w$ and $\bar u$ both map to $\bar v$; this respects transition maps, and via step 1 it is the map induced by $g$ on algebraic-space stalks, since $bh=ga$. Thus both composites send every representing germ to the same pulled-back germ.

source.place: Tag 04NG (lemma-flat-at-point-etale-local-rings), chosen presentation and local-ring square; Tag 05VN for the specified lift, and spaces.tex Tag 02X1 for presentations.

proof.text: The induced homomorphism $A^{\mathrm{sh}}\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is local. Indeed the evaluations $\epsilon_Y:A^{\mathrm{sh}}\to\Omega$ and $\epsilon_X:B^{\mathrm{sh}}\to\Omega$ have the maximal ideals as their kernels by step 2. On a regular-function representative, pulling back along $h$ and then evaluating at $\bar u$ is evaluation at $h\bar u=\bar v$. Hence $\epsilon_X\circ g^\sharp=\epsilon_Y$. It follows that $(g^\sharp)^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{B^{\mathrm{sh}}})=\mathfrak m_{A^{\mathrm{sh}}}$; in particular $g^\sharp$ sends the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal, as required. The chart-stalk maps used here preserve evaluation by step 1, so this calculation is for the stipulated map on algebraic-space stalks.

source.place: Tag 04KJ (lemma-morphism-locally-ringed), localness on geometric stalks; the evaluation-kernel proof uses the already established chart identifications.

proof.text: By step 2, $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are, as $A$- and $B$-algebras, the triples colimits over the local rings $A$ and $B$ at their maximal ideals, and strict henselizations in the sense of [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Apply [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] to the local rings $A$ and $B$. In particular $B\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is faithfully flat. If $B$ is flat over $A$, transitivity [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] makes $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ flat over $A$. Conversely, if $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is flat over $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-algebra-faithfully-flat-descent] applied to $A\to B\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ makes $B$ flat over $A$. Finally [lem-sfb-strict-henselization-module-flatness], applied to the $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$-module $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ in the commutative square of step 3, gives flatness over $A$ if and only if flatness over $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Therefore $h$ is flat at $u$ exactly when the stipulated map $\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}\to\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ is flat, by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. This holds for every compatible chart and every $u$ over $x$, while step 3 supplies at least one. It follows that the existential chart definition is equivalent to flatness of the stipulated stalk map, proving geometricStalk_flat_iff. The separate declaration flatAt_iff_chart_stalk is proved directly in steps 6-8 below.

source.place: Tag 04NG (lemma-flat-at-point-etale-local-rings), final paragraph, using 07QM, algebra.tex 039V and flat.tex 05VL.

proof.text: For flatAt_iff_chart_stalk use a direct refinement argument, independent of the three preceding strict-local assertions. First prove that PointRepresentative.Rel [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes] is an equivalence: reflexivity and symmetry use identity and exchanged maps. For transitivity, two common fields over the middle representative have a nonempty scheme fibre product over its field spectrum; a residue field at a point of this fibre product gives a common extension, and the presheaf composition law transports the two equalities. Existence of the point is Scheme.exists_preimage_of_isPullback from the fibre-product point description [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points]. Thus Quot.eqvGen_exact and Equivalence.eqvGen_iff turn equality of two scheme image classes into an actual common-field agreement. Evaluate the represented presheaf pullback on that field: Types.exists_of_isPullback lifts the compatible maps, and the unique points of the field spectra map to the two prescribed scheme points.

source.place: Tag 03BU, common-field equivalence of points; Tag 03H4, lemma-points-cartesian; Tag 01JT, points of a fibre product.

proof.text: In a commutative square of scheme maps a h = k b with a and b etale, compare the flatness of the two horizontal stalk maps at w and a(w). Precomposition with a does not change flatness: its stalk map is flat and local, hence faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-algebra-faithfully-flat-descent] proves descent, and composition of flat ring maps proves ascent. Postcomposition with b does not change flatness by [lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness], applied to the source stalk as a module over the intermediate stalk. Scheme.Hom.stalkMap_comp expresses both comparisons; rewriting along the square equality gives the horizontal equivalence.

source.place: Descent lemma-flat-at-point; Flat Modules Tag 05BA, lemma-etale-flat-up-down-local-ring.

proof.text: Unpack the existential chart witness U′ -> V′ of MapIsFlatAt [def-sfb-space-flat-at-point]. Scheme-test etaleness [def-trf-algebraic-space] represents W = U times_X U′ and Z = V times_Y V′. Both projections of each square are etale: comparing a given representing square with the one supplied by the opposite etale chart gives a unique Yoneda isomorphism, and scheme etaleness respects that isomorphism. The preceding common-field argument gives w in W over the two prescribed points. The two original chart equations induce k : W -> Z by the pullback universal property. Its two projection equations give commutative etale source-and-target squares with both original chart maps. Apply the preceding scheme stalk equivalence to each square and compose the equivalences to transfer flatness from the witness to the specified chart. Conversely the specified chart and its assumed flat stalk map are directly a witness for MapIsFlatAt. No surjectivity of the charts or finiteness of the spaces is used.
